authority_order.description: Pack Groovy is the first construction authority whenever it performs the registration itself.
SuSyCore Java is used when Groovy only binds an existing object or has no constructor surface.
Pack configuration, resources, and external-mod data are used only when neither Groovy nor SuSyCore owns the construction.

families.label: Materials and generated fluids
families.description: GT materials, including liquid and gas forms, are declared centrally and built in category register methods.
families.lifecycle: MaterialEvent at LOWEST after SuSyCore's HIGH listener

authority_chain.note: SuSyMaterials.init() calls category register() methods; each category assigns a new Material.Builder to the central field.
SuSyCore registers its baseline materials first; pack-owned additions prefer Groovy.

families.label: Elements and isotopes
families.description: Element identities and isotope-backed materials are constructed during the material lifecycle.

authority_chain.note: Groovy constructs Element objects and their Material.Builder registrations.
Core owns only the Java baseline not already supplied by the pack scripts.

families.label: Material flags and custom properties
families.description: Existing materials are modified and SuSy-specific fiber/fluid property types are attached.

authority_chain.note: Groovy registers the base property type and applies pack flag/property changes.
Core defines the custom Java property and icon types consumed by Groovy.

families.label: Simple meta-items
families.description: Pack-only simple items use a StandardMetaItem created from Groovy and numeric addItem registrations.

authority_chain.note: Simple pack components are registered with new StandardMetaItem(2) and addItem(id, name).
Behavior-bearing items and Core-owned components remain Java registrations.

families.label: GregTech machine recipes
families.description: Machine recipes are built in domain-organized postInit scripts against named recipe-map aliases.

authority_chain.note: Scripts call MAP.recipeBuilder(), add typed inputs/outputs, duration and EUt, then buildAndRegister().
Java recipes are reserved for Core mechanics that cannot be expressed as ordinary pack recipes.

families.label: Crafting and smelting recipes
families.description: Shaped, shapeless, replacement, and smelting recipes are authored through GroovyScript managers.

authority_chain.note: The pack uses crafting.add/replace methods and smelting managers alongside domain recipes.
Core supplies only mechanics-coupled recipe registrations.

families.label: Recipe removal, replacement, and JEI policy
families.description: Pack overhauls remove recipes by name/input and hide displaced categories or ingredients.

authority_chain.note: Groovy owns removeAllRecipes, removeByInput, crafting.remove, replacement, and JEI yeet/hide calls.

families.label: Recipe maps, builders, and properties
families.description: Groovy resolves recipe-map names, but SuSyCore constructs the maps and any custom builders/properties.
families.lifecycle: SuSyCore static initialization; Groovy prePostInit binding

authority_chain.note: recipemap(name) is an alias lookup and does not create a RecipeMap.
Core constructs RecipeMap objects, slot limits, UI, sound, builders, and typed properties.

families.label: Ore dictionary and unification entries
families.description: Pack entries, removals, and aliases are centralized in Groovy; generated Core forms use Java loaders.
families.lifecycle: prePostInit Groovy; Forge recipe registry event in Core

authority_chain.note: Ordinary add/remove relationships use ore(name).add/remove in the pack's central script.
Core registers generated material blocks and mechanics-bound entries.

families.label: Thermodynamic process families
families.description: Coolants, cryogenic gases, refrigerants, fuels, and working-fluid families expand into recipes from Groovy data objects.

authority_chain.note: Reusable Groovy classes hold parameters and register related recipe sets.

families.label: Gameplay and horde events
families.description: Pack gameplay events use Groovy to instantiate SuSyCore event APIs and attach triggers/modifiers.

authority_chain.note: Groovy constructs MobHordeEvent and other pack policy against Core APIs.
Core defines reusable mechanics rather than individual pack events.

families.label: Loot-table tweaks
families.description: Loot additions and removals are registered in the pack's gameplay Groovy scripts.

authority_chain.note: The script targets named loot tables and pools through GroovyScript integrations.

families.label: Blocks and ItemBlocks
families.description: SuSy blocks are Java VariantBlock classes discovered by SuSyBlocks and registered in Forge block/item events.

authority_chain.note: The observed pack has no Groovy block registry constructor.
VariantBlock fields are instantiated, registry-named, block-registered, ItemBlock-registered, and model-registered.

families.label: Stone types and ore prefixes
families.description: New generated GT form families and SuSy stone types are Java API registrations.

authority_chain.note: Groovy consumes these identities but does not construct the registered prefix/type objects.
Core defines prefixes/types and adds generated meta-item prefixes after materials.

families.label: Custom fluid storage keys and attributes
families.description: Nonstandard fluid states and behavior attributes are defined and registered in SuSyCore.

authority_chain.note: Groovy attaches and queries Core-defined storage keys.
Core owns storage-key identity, generated variants, attributes, and tooltip behavior.

families.label: Behavior-bearing items and armor
families.description: Items with capabilities, armor logic, renderers, or Core behavior are Java meta-items.
families.lifecycle: SuSyCore item initialization and Forge item registry

authority_chain.note: Groovy remains suitable only when the item is a simple StandardMetaItem entry.
Core attaches behavior, armor logic, capability components, and client rendering.

families.label: Forge tile entities
families.description: Non-GT block entities are registered by SuSyCore with stable resource locations and optional renderers.

authority_chain.note: No Groovy tile-entity registry surface was observed.
Core calls GameRegistry.registerTileEntity and binds client renderers.

families.label: GT single-block machines
families.description: Single-block machine MTEs are Java classes and numeric registrations in SuSyMetaTileEntities.

authority_chain.note: Groovy scripts add recipes to machines but do not register MTEs.
Core defines the class/recipe behavior and calls registerMetaTileEntity with an allocated ID.

families.label: GT multiblock machines
families.description: Multiblocks require Java controllers, block-pattern predicates, abilities, recipe maps, and MTE registration.

authority_chain.note: Recipes are Groovy-authored, but controller/pattern registration is not.
Core owns structure patterns, controller logic, registration IDs, abilities, and render behavior.

families.label: Multiblock parts, abilities, and capabilities
families.description: Custom buses, hatches, ability registries, and capabilities are SuSyCore Java surfaces.
families.lifecycle: Core static initialization and capability setup

authority_chain.note: No Groovy ability/capability constructor surface was observed.
Core registers capability interfaces and MTE parts that expose multiblock abilities.

families.label: GT cover behaviors
families.description: Covers bind a stable resource ID and meta-item to a Java behavior factory.

authority_chain.note: The observed pack does not register cover behaviors in Groovy.
Core calls registerBehavior with item and factory identities.

families.label: Forge and Immersive Railroading entities
families.description: Gameplay entities and their renderers are registered from SuSyCore Java.

authority_chain.note: Groovy spawns existing entity classes but does not register new entity types.
Core registers entity resource IDs, numeric tracking IDs, factories, and client renderers.

families.label: Biomes
families.description: SuSyCore constructs biome classes/properties and registers them through Forge.

authority_chain.note: No Groovy biome constructor surface was observed.
Core creates BiomeProperties, assigns registry names, registers biomes, and adds dictionary types.

families.label: Dimensions, planets, and celestial objects
families.description: Core registers dimension types and planet layout, while celestial object graphs provide dimension identities.

authority_chain.note: The observed Groovy globals only reference existing dimension IDs.
Core constructs DimensionType, Planet, celestial identities, biome layout, sky, gravity, and registration.
GregTech configuration admits dimension IDs but does not replace Core planet registration.

families.label: Sound events
families.description: SuSyCore constructs and registers SoundEvent identities used by machines, blocks, entities, and items.

authority_chain.note: Groovy consumes sound-bearing maps but does not register sound events.
Core creates SoundEvent, sets registry names, registers with Forge, and supplies sound assets metadata.

families.label: Physics particles and client effects
families.description: Physics particle identities and rendered client particle effects are SuSyCore Java types.

authority_chain.note: No Groovy particle registry constructor was observed.
Core constructs particle-domain objects, registers them, and implements visual effects.

families.label: Network packets and GT modules
families.description: SuSyCore owns module-container and packet registrations required by mechanics.

authority_chain.note: No Groovy packet or module registration surface was observed.
Core registers the GT module container and packet classes.

families.label: Server commands and subcommands
families.description: SuSyCore constructs and registers horde, faction, recipe-map dump, and untranslated-key server commands.

authority_chain.note: No pack Groovy server-command constructor was observed.
Core instantiates ICommand implementations during serverStarting, registers roots, and attaches horde subcommands.

families.label: Optional-mod integration registrations
families.description: SuSyCore modules register integration-owned items, tile entities, IR entities and GUI types, JEI categories, OpenComputers drivers/floppies, and probe providers.
families.lifecycle: SuSyCore construction through postInit and optional-mod module events

authority_chain.note: Pack Groovy adds recipes and policy for existing integrations but does not construct their Java registry types.
Core owns optional-mod module classes, registry callbacks, drivers, plugins, GUI/container bindings, and providers.

families.label: Rocket components and blueprints
families.description: Rocket component, fuel, stage, and blueprint domain types are Core mechanics backed by registered blocks/items/entities.

authority_chain.note: Groovy adds progression recipes for existing rocket components.
Core defines the runtime component/blueprint model and registered content.

families.label: GregTech ore veins and fluid deposits
families.description: Pack worldgen deposits are JSON definitions consumed directly by GregTech.

authority_chain.note: No Groovy deposit constructor is used by the observed pack.
Core supplies related materials/blocks but does not own these deposit definitions.
Each JSON file is the formal vein or bedrock-fluid registration consumed by GregTech.

families.label: Gaspunk gases and agents
families.description: Custom atmospheric gases and health agents are external-mod JSON data owned by the pack.

authority_chain.note: Groovy integrates recipes and existing gas identities but does not define the gas registry records.
SuSyCore does not construct Gaspunk custom gas records.
Gaspunk loads these JSON records directly.

families.label: External spawn and loot rules
families.description: InControl JSON owns pack rules for potential spawns, spawn admission, experience, and external loot.

authority_chain.note: These global external-mod rule tables are not registered by Groovy.
Core's MobHordeEvent is a separate scripted-event path.
InControl reads the ordered JSON rules directly.

families.label: Quests and progression
families.description: BetterQuesting quest lines, quest records, rewards, and tasks are pack JSON data.

authority_chain.note: Groovy recipes support progression but do not construct the quest database.
SuSyCore does not own BetterQuesting records.
BetterQuesting consumes the ID-linked JSON database.

families.label: Structures and generation rules
families.description: Recurrent Complex structure, inventory-generator, transformer, and placement records are binary/data assets in the pack.

authority_chain.note: No Groovy structure registry constructor is used.
Core may consume structures but does not define these Recurrent Complex records.
Recurrent Complex loads the pack's structure and generator records directly.

families.label: Localization, models, textures, and resource overrides
families.description: Resource Loader supplies pack-owned translations and visual assets, including companions for Groovy meta-items.

authority_chain.note: Groovy creates identities whose client representation is supplied by resource data.
Core ships assets for Java-owned content inside its JAR.
Resource Loader applies these files directly from the installed instance.

patterns.label: Material-backed fluid
patterns.summary: Allocate a petrochemistry material ID and update SuSyMaterials, PetrochemistryMaterials, and central English localization.

questions.label: Developer name
questions.description: Human-readable name used to derive registry and Groovy symbol identities.

questions.label: English translation
questions.description: Display name; defaults to the developer name.

questions.label: Groovy symbol
questions.description: Central static-field symbol; defaults to PascalCase name and can preserve acronym casing.

limitations: This first material pattern intentionally matches the observed petrochemistry liquid convention and adds FLAMMABLE.
The updated scripts still require a Cleanroom launch to prove runtime registration.

patterns.label: GregTech machine recipe
patterns.summary: Append one structured recipeBuilder chain to an existing domain-organized postInit script using an observed Recipemaps alias.

questions.label: Owning postInit script
questions.description: Existing script whose domain owns this recipe.

questions.label: Recipe map alias
questions.description: Uppercase alias formally resolved in prePostInit/Recipemaps.groovy.

questions.label: Item inputs
questions.description: Ore, meta-item, or item stacks consumed by the recipe.

questions.label: Item outputs
questions.description: Ore, meta-item, or item stacks produced by the recipe.

limitations: The V1 renderer covers ordinary item/fluid inputs and outputs, duration, and EUt; specialized builder properties remain future patterns.
Recipe-map slot arity is not yet proven before launch, so the wizard reports that runtime check as outstanding.

patterns.label: Ore dictionary entry
patterns.summary: Append an ore(name).add(...) relationship to Supersymmetry's central prePostInit oreDict script.

questions.label: Ore dictionary name
questions.description: Forge ore dictionary key to receive the entry.

questions.label: Registered ingredient
questions.description: One existing ore, meta-item, or item identity.

limitations: This pattern adds one relationship and does not hide or remove displaced JEI ingredients.
